question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{1}{3}y=6 \\ 5x-y=4\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.

$x=$
{{field-1}}$,\,y=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
To get rid of the fractions in the first equation, we must multiply the first equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $3.$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{1}{3}y=6 & |\,\times 3 \\ 5x-y=4\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}6x+y=18 \\ 5x-y=4\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that the $y$ term in the first equation can cancel with the $-y$ term in the second equation.

Adding the two equations eliminates the $y$-variable, and allows us to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6x+\cancel{y} & =18 \\ 5x-\cancel{y} & =4 \\ 11x & =22 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can substitute $x=2$ into the equation $6x+y=18$ to solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6x+y & =18 \\ 6\cdot 2+y & =18 \\ 12+y & =18 \\ y & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=2,\,y=6.$
